B.mode: persistent PyTorch CPU BF16-storage/FP32-manual-cast TE overlapped with GPU denoise

C.mode: persistent OpenVINO BF16 CPU TE overlapped with GPU denoise

D.mode: persistent OpenVINO INT8 CPU TE overlapped with GPU denoise

overlap_interpretation.B: real overlap (37.1 s) but CPU encode 137-208 s per prompt dwarfs 12-13 s denoise; GPU idle 124-196 s each cycle; CPU-bound.
overlap_interpretation.C: OpenVINO BF16 encode 0.40-0.77 s fully hidden inside 12-13 s GPU denoise; GPU-bound.
overlap_interpretation.D: OpenVINO INT8 encode 0.36-0.63 s fully hidden; GPU-bound; lower worker RSS and larger conditioning error.

contention.finding: No measurable GPU slowdown from 16-thread CPU encoding; B/C/D generation stays within ~1 s of A. The CPU work is hidden or the bottleneck, not a GPU-throttling source.

vram.note: Pipeline B/C/D use the same precomputed-cond DiT/VAE graph as the E2E precomputed arms, so the E2E VRAM measurement applies; GPU encoder allocation is absent.

analysis.break_even: TE-only speedup is 200-500x, but E2E throughput is bounded by ~12-13 s denoise. A CPU TE faster than GPU TE buys at most ~0.5-1 s/request (4-8%) once it is hidden; the large cold-start gain in this session also includes avoiding a 16.8 GB GPU CLIP reload.
